summary: Agent CLI exposes host shell and self-upgrade to a configurable WebSocket server
details: The package ships a CLI agent that, on startup, opens a WebSocket to a configured server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL / configuration file). The message router in the agent treats inbound frames as authoritative commands over the installer's host: `terminal_create` spawns a shell PTY and subsequent `terminal_input` frames are passed directly to `pty.write`, yielding arbitrary shell execution on the host under the operator's account. Additional server-driven handlers perform filesystem writes, git commit/push, MCP/LLM reconfiguration, and an `upgrade_agent` path that writes a 0o755 `upgrade.sh` into the user's config directory and shells out to `npm install <pkgName>@latest` followed by a restart, using a package name taken from runtime context. Whoever controls the WebSocket endpoint the CLI is pointed at can therefore execute commands, modify files, and force a package reinstall on the host without any local prompt at the time of the action. The destination server is operator-configurable rather than a hardcoded attacker endpoint, and the behavior is broadly the CLI's advertised purpose, but the full-host RCE and reinstall surface are exposed to whichever server the CLI ends up connected to (including a misconfigured or hijacked one).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
